This project (ai-lab-memory) is the knowledge memory system for an AI-Lab mesh infrastructure consisting of three nodes (Hanzo, Sariatu, and Kubo) with multiple interconnected components. The main architecture includes: Erudito v3 as the knowledge orchestration agent with modular architecture (core business logic + integrations), registry-centric design with YAML + Redis dual-write; LiteLLM proxy (port 4000 on Hanzo, port 4001 on Kubo) providing unified model access to Max (Haiku), OpenAI Pro, Opencode Zen (legacy credit), Opencode Go (subscription), and laptop models; NotebookLM MCP (31 tools) as consultant/validator; Qdrant for vector storage; env-masker for secret masking; OpenClaw running on Kubo with direct OAuth to OpenAI Pro; and Aegis as an in-development supply chain defense system.

This is a personal AI-Lab infrastructure project run by a single user (r0calex) across multiple machines (Hanzo as main, Sariatu as secondary, Kubo as satellite). It provides a self-hosted AI development environment with unified model access through LiteLLM, knowledge management through Erudito with NotebookLM validation, secret masking through env-masker, and supply-chain security through Aegis. The system is designed for mesh-wide access to premium models (Max Haiku, OpenAI Pro) without per-token costs through subscriptions. Quality standards are strict: once deployed, the quality level becomes the minimum and must never regress. All projects are documented with specs, plans, implementation reports (IRs), and standard operating procedures (SOPs), stored either in claude_contracts/ or within the project repos themselves (like Aegis docs inside ~/ai-lab/aegis/docs/).

External dependencies and integrations include: Anthropic Max (for Haiku models via API, not Sonnet/Opus which are API-restricted); OpenAI Pro via OAuth (for openai-codex/gpt-5.4) and paid API key (for LiteLLM); Opencode.ai Zen endpoint (legacy credit pool) and Go endpoint (subscription with fallback to credit); NotebookLM MCP (31 tools); Qdrant vector database; Redis; LiteLLM as the unified gateway; OpenClaw agent framework; security-guidance Claude plugin; and Grype/Syft (Anchore) for OCI vulnerability scanning (Trivy explicitly prohibited due to supply-chain compromise).
